sentences.text: Researchers created a human oligodendrocyte cell model of Krabbe disease by using CRISPR technology to remove the GALC gene. These modified cells exhibited significantly lower GALC enzyme activity and accumulated high levels of the lipids psychosine and lactosylceramide compared to normal cells.

Brain and heart tissue from twitcher mice also showed increased lactosylceramide levels, and the study found that these changes were connected to altered activity in the AKT cellular signaling pathway in both the cells and the mice. The authors conclude that lactosylceramide buildup is a consistent feature of GALC deficiency across these human cell and animal models.
